chose: implement the recipe-enrichment plan as one branch, coordinating Sonnet sub-agents over disjoint file sets
because: the plan decomposes cleanly into disjoint file sets (packages/food, pipeline-contract, the migration, the kernel primitive), so parallel agents in one working tree cannot collide; worktrees would cost a merge per agent for no isolation benefit

chose: set RECIPE_ENRICHMENT_MAX_IN_FLIGHT on the Railway 'pipeline' service only
over: setting it on pipeline and pipeline-worker as plan §11 says
because: grep shows globalConcurrency() is read only by reconcile.ts and server.ts, both server-process code; ATPROTO_SYNC_MAX_IN_FLIGHT follows the same rule in .railway/railway.ts today. A variable on the worker that nothing reads reads as configuration and is not.

chose: run 'railway config plan' and 'railway config apply' for the .railway/railway.ts changes
because: no Backboard token in this cloud session — 'railway config plan' fails with 'Backboard token is required for plan.'. The config file itself evaluates clean (railway CLI reports ok:true for the evaluate step), so the change is syntactically and structurally valid; applying it needs a human with Railway credentials.

chose: extend traits.json with a curated 'tg' tag map (meat/pork/alcohol/seafood) beside vg/vt/al
over: hardcoding pork and alcohol slug lists inside classifiers/diet.ts
shipping only the {vg,vt,al} shape plan §4.1 sketches
because: plan §8.2 asks for halal/kosher pork+alcohol exclusion and for pescatarian to tell meat from fish, and §4.1's three keys answer none of those. The taxonomy already encodes the hierarchy that reaches en:pancetta from en:pork, and the accumulating ancestor-closure fold §4.1 builds for allergens folds tags identically — a slug list in the classifier would restate that hierarchy by hand and rot the first time OFF adds a cured-pork node.

chose: packages/food/src/lexicon.json is checked in pretty-printed, but scripts/build-food-lexicon.ts emits it compact — regenerating produces a 10,718-line diff whose data is byte-identical after JSON normalization
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes

lint-staged runs 'oxfmt' over '*.json' on every commit, so the generated compact file is re-pretty-printed by the pre-commit hook before it ever lands, and every checked-in generated JSON in this repo is the hook's output rather than the generator's
discriminatedBy: stage the regenerated lexicon.json, run the pre-commit hook, and diff the result against HEAD: an empty diff confirms the hook is the reformatter; a surviving diff means the checked-in blob came from somewhere else

chose: lint-staged's oxfmt over '*.json' is the reformatter: every generated JSON in this repo is checked in as the pre-commit hook's output, not the generator's, so a regenerated file only looks changed until it is formatted
because: ran 'npx oxfmt packages/food/src/lexicon.json' over the freshly regenerated compact output; 'git diff --stat packages/food/src/lexicon.json' then came back empty — the formatter reproduces the checked-in blob exactly

chose: the dev corpus resolves 396/396 ingredient lines to a food slug — 0% unresolved, where the plan expected the unresolved share to be the number deciding whether phase 2 is worth it
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
the corpus is the repo's own curated dev seed, which exists to calibrate this matcher, so it is not an independent sample of what the network writes
discriminatedBy: run the same measurement over recipes rendered by an atproto-sync sweep of the live network, which nobody curated against this lexicon, and compare the unresolved share

because: an independently sampled corpus — a census of all 210 recipes from the 39 non-bulk-import DIDs — measured 213/1745 = 12.2% unresolved against the dev seed's 0/396. Per stratum the bulk importer's 3695 Wikibooks rows measure 3.81% and its 346 machine-styled rows 2.78%, so which population you ask about moves the answer 4x. Every headline number was independently re-derived from the committed seed with the real matcher, and the classifier re-run end-to-end reproduced 219/977/0/904 bit-for-bit. Caveat: the stratum boundary was drawn with those per-stratum rates already known (d-64be66fe), though it selected the HIGHER-miss stratum and rests on a provenance argument that stands without them.

chose: devtools recipe inspector renders generic DebugSection {table, note, published, rows}, not a typed view per table
over: a typed panel section per table (recipe_meta, recipe_enrichment, household_recipe, ...)
because: counted the private sidecars this recipe schema already carries — recipe_meta, household_recipe_meta, household_recipe, household_recipe_note, recipe_collection_entry, meal_plan_entry, recipe_pending_image, recipe_enrichment, recipe_enrichment_label: nine, and it has grown one every plan or two. A typed section per table makes every future sidecar a UI change; a generic section makes it one server-side query. The 'published' flag carries the only distinction a reader actually needs.

chose: the devtools panel reads the active recipe id from router state
over: an EventClient (@tanstack/devtools-event-client) that the recipe route emits into
because: TanStackDevtools is rendered inside the router tree in __root.tsx, so router hooks already know which recipe is open. The event client is the right tool when a LIBRARY pushes state the shell cannot otherwise see; here it would be a second source of truth for a fact the router already holds, plus a subscription to leak.

chose: delete EnrichmentDebugPanel; the devtools plugin supersedes it
over: keeping both the pinned overlay and the devtools tab
because: the overlay was a stopgap from the enrichment plan §10 and already needed one fix for rendering illegibly over the recipe. The devtools tab shows strictly more (raw atproto record, counterparts, every private layer) and shows it somewhere that is not on top of the page being debugged. Two dev surfaces for the same data is how one of them goes stale.

chose: no additional devtools plugins: not the @tanstack ones for absent libraries, and no third-party ones
because: counted the instances before adding the mechanism. Form, Table, Pacer, Virtual, Store, DB and Ranger have ZERO matches in pnpm-lock.yaml — a panel for a library the app does not use is dead weight. Re-run the query with: grep -c '@tanstack/react-form' pnpm-lock.yaml. Router and Query devtools are already wired and are the complete set; router-devtools 1.167.1 IS npm latest despite looking stale next to router 1.170.30 (peerDeps satisfied). The two third-party candidates were put to the user with downloads, age, maintainer count and bundle impact, and both were declined — server-functions for being a 4-version single-maintainer package, better-auth-devtools for not being a TanStack plugin at all and needing a devtools() plugin in the auth server config.

chose: sparse enrichment labels: store only what differs from a documented per-dimension default
over: the dense encoding — one row per (recipe, dimension, slug) for all 23 slugs
dropping only the six structural macro-diet slugs and keeping dense otherwise
because: measured 828 rows over 36 recipes: 34.8% not_detected, 33.5% unknown, only 23.8% actionable. The Randomizer's exclusion scan reads contains/may_contain/excluded and never touches the rest, so dense storage bought nothing and grows with the corpus. Re-run with: select verdict, count(*) from recipe_enrichment_label group by verdict. Allergen unknown still earns a row — it is the one negative that differs from the default (not_detected = read every line and found nothing; unknown = could not read every line), and collapsing both into absence would lose the distinction this feature is most careful about.

chose: delete the macro-dependent diet rules, paleo, and the halal/kosher no-rule-can-certify unknown; keep their recipe_vocab slugs
over: leaving them emitting a constant unknown until phase 2
also deleting the six slugs from recipe_vocab
because: each emitted the same verdict for every recipe in the database — 216 of 828 rows restating a constant. The vocab rows must stay: keto, low_carb, low_fat, low_calorie, diabetic and paleo are upstream exchange.recipe.defs#diet* tokens with recipe_vocab_alias rows from 1785300000000_create_recipe_rendered.ts, and render.ts's resolveToken maps them for AUTHOR-DECLARED diets on recipe.suitable_for_diet — deleting them would break the sync path. The halal/kosher caveat is true and now assumed: somebody keeping kosher either keeps a kitchen to spec or does not, and knows they must source certified ingredients either way.
